summary: Is the FULL 9x->1x GDN state-HBM reduction reachable on OUR battle-tested replay/sequential-rank-1 tree-scan kernel (WY OUT OF SCOPE)? Exact per-forward traffic accounting (is stage-1 accept-only-publish only partial, what number?), then the full route: eliminate the kernel scratch store via store-small-activations + replay-accepted-next-step with IDENTICAL op order (bit-exact), preserving batch-invariance + capture. CPU, no GPU.

synthesis.stage1_exact_reduction:
**Stage-1 (accept-only durable publish) is a 1.385x total GDN-state-traffic cut at nominal a=4 — NOT 9x->1x.** Exact accounting (row = 48vh x 128 x 128 fp32 = 3.146 MB; 48 GDN layers x B=4 = 192 (layer,req) pairs = 0.604 GB/forward per row-touch; a = accepted-path rows, nominal 4):

- CURRENT (HEAD, all-rows publish at scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:2751-2755): 2a+28 rows/layer/req = kernel scratch write 9 (N_ACTUAL=9, mask fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:352 — NOT N_PAD=16) + publish 9R+9W=18 + next-step remap 2a + h0 read 1. At a=4: **36 rows = 21.74 GB/forward** (~80% of the 27 GB weight stream). Actual native E5 (source-verified fused_sigmoid_gating in-loop per-token stores) = 1R+6W = 7 rows = 4.23 GB → CURRENT = **5.14x actual native** (the FR13 doc's "9.0x" was vs an idealized 2-row native and under-counted touches).
- AFTER stage-1 (codex working-tree diff: deferred publish :2752-2761 + committer accept-only index_copy_ :3649-3690/:4014-4055; kernel store + remap UNCHANGED): 4a+10 rows best (6a+10 if the index_select temp spills cache). At a=4: **26 rows = 15.70 GB/forward**.
- **Exact factor: 36/26 = 1.385x at a=4** (1.78x at a=2, 1.55x at a=3, 1.27x at a=5); removes 2(9-a) = 10 rows = 6.04 GB/forward. On the doc's own scale: ~9x -> ~6.5x; vs actual native: 5.14x -> 3.71x. Only the publish stream itself shrinks 18 -> 2a (2.25x). Red-team floor: at a=5 with a spilled temp, stage-1 is net NEGATIVE (38->40 rows, 0.95x).
- Untouched by stage-1: kernel scratch store 5.44 GB, remap 4.83 GB, h0 0.60 GB. Theoretical floor (kernel store gone, single-row commit) = 1R+1W = 2 rows = 1.21 GB/forward + ~0.2-0.4 GB activation epsilon — actual native E5 is itself 3.5x above that ideal.
synthesis.full_route:
**Full ~1.0x route = activation-store + accepted-path REPLAY on OUR existing sequential rank-1 tree kernel (WY out of scope).**

WHAT IS STORED (exactly what the scan consumed, at consumed precision — per node ~16.2 KiB bf16 vs 3 MiB state row, ~190x smaller; ~50 MiB persistent total at B=4 x 48 layers x 16 nodes): k = key_spec slice PRE-l2norm (patch :2466), v = value_tree slice (:2467), raw_a/raw_b (:2470-2471). A_log/dt_bias are persistent params; q NOT needed (q-side ops :334/:336/:342 never touch state; out already emitted during the scan). Under RAW_GATING the g/beta tensor loads (:303-312) are dead. Store into a PREALLOCATED per-layer ring buffer (graph-stable address, visible to vLLM memory profiling) — not by-reference pinning of forward intermediates.

KERNEL CHANGES: (1) add STORE_NODE_STATES constexpr to _tree_gdn_kernel, skip the per-node HBM export at fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:349-353 (it is a pure export — children read h_cache registers :277-286, never the store — so deleting it cannot perturb the scan); delete the 201.3 MB/layer tree_state_all torch.empty (patch :2020-2030, the capture-blocking alloc). (2) NEW replay kernel = chain-specialized sibling: no h_cache (spill-free at any tree size, sidesteps the N_PAD=16 spill), one (BLOCK_V=16, DIM_K=128) register tile, static_range over MAX_PATH_LEN with t<accepted_len masking; per step: indirect-load node = accepted_path[b,t], load k/v/raw_a/raw_b from the activation store, recompute decay/beta/l2norm intermediates (:314-335), apply `state += 0.0` for t>=1 (the ±0.0 handoff normalization — see proof field), run the IDENTICAL :338-341 update, store post-step state to bank linear column t. Whole path fold in ONE kernel (per-program read-h0-tile-before-write makes publish-overwrites-h0-row safe; per-step launches would not be).

BIT-EXACTNESS MECHANISM: same h0 bank bytes (publish is deferred — nothing writes spec rows between the scan's h0 read :261-266/patch :2474-2480 and the committer, verified :3047/:3175 are non-spec prefill), same stored input bytes, same fp32 instruction sequence in the native gate-folding basis (NOT rescaled — the GB10 exp-blowup caveat) → IEEE-754 determinism gives identical bits, conditional only on codegen identity: factor :288-343 into one shared @triton.jit body used by both kernels, same constexprs (DIM_K=128/BLOCK_V=16) and num_warps=8, gated by a one-time byte A/B on captured payloads (FR10_TREE_GDN_CAPTURE_PAYLOAD harness, patch :2683-2739, already saves h0+inputs+serving_state).

WHERE IT PLUGS: Option 1 (minimal, eager) — replace the committer publish index_copy_ at :3683-3686 (greedy) and :4048-4051 (sampled) with the replay launch; same launch count as today. Option 2 (final, graph-capturable) — fuse as the NEXT-step prologue: keep launch_tree_state_linear_remap's conv branch (kernel :195-203, the FR13 conv-prior-window carrier — must NOT be deleted), replace the ssm branch (:186-194) with the replay writing linear columns directly; needs a one-event-delayed accepted-lens buffer to locate h0's column (prev_len-1). Inputs (accepted_paths/lens) already live in persistent device buffers sized to decode_cudagraph_max_bs (patch :184-201) — the proven static-shape pattern (remap mask :100-101, h0 in-kernel tl.load :261-266).

TRAFFIC RESULT at a=4: scan h0 1R + replay h0 1R + replay writes a = 2+a = **6 rows = 3.62 GB/forward = 0.86x actual native E5 (4.23 GB)**; with single-row commit (needs a live-container consumer audit — only column accepted_len-1 is provably read) = 3 rows = 1.81 GB. Either lands at/below the ~1.0x-native target. Replay FLOPs ~5-33 µs vs the ~99 ms weight-bound forward — free. Optional cheap stage-2 en route: publish to LINEAR columns so the remap becomes identity (saves another 2a rows = 4.83 GB).
synthesis.bitexact_and_bi_proof:
**Why replay-identical-op-order survives the objection that killed delta-only:** delta-only stored per-node deltas and RECONSTRUCTED S_path = (prod exp(g_j))·h0 + sum_j (prod_{l>j} exp(g_l))·Delta_j — ℝ-equal but fp32-DIFFERENT because it REASSOCIATES the decay products and sums relative to the scan's interleaved multiply-then-rank-1 sequence (the rescaled-basis class, FR13_LOSSLESS_FAST_DERIVATION.md:57-59, and the FR12 5.96e-8 op-order family; Delta_j also depends on the RUNNING state, so re-derivation changes rounding). Replay does not reconstruct — it RE-EXECUTES the identical instruction sequence on bit-identical inputs; IEEE-754 ops are deterministic functions of (input bits, rounding mode). This distinction was verified rigorously, not by assertion: the scan (kernel :268-353) was confirmed line-by-line to be a pure fp32 register chain from h0 (h_cache select :280-286, last surviving tl.where = immediate parent's exact register value; the :349-353 HBM store is export-only, never an input).

**Proof obligations (the conditional parts, each with a gate):** (1) ±0.0 normalization — the parent-handoff tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j, h_cache, 0.0)) (:282-285) flips -0.0 to +0.0 once per edge; replay must apply `state += 0.0` per handoff AFTER the root (root i=0 has an empty j-loop → no normalization of h0). N_PAD-independent. (2) Inputs at consumed precision — byte-copy the bf16 k/v/raw_a/raw_b; the fp32 widening cast is exact. (3) Recomputed intermediates (softplus incl. the x<=20 branch :325-329, sigmoid :331, k-l2norm rsqrt(sum+1e-6) :335, exp(b_g) :338) are pure per-node functions of stored inputs + persistent weights — same formula on same bits, same libdevice → same bits. (4) Codegen identity is NOT spec-guaranteed (FMA contraction/scheduling per unrolled instance) — mitigated by one shared @triton.jit body + identical constexprs/num_warps, PROVEN by the one-time empirical byte A/B (torch bit-equality, all 48 layers, all accepted lens, including a -0.0-in-parent case and a publish-dst==h0-row case). (5) Bank-dtype cast at final store must match torch RTNE (identity if bank fp32 per mamba_ssm_dtype=float32; verified in the A/B).

**Batch-invariance preserved by construction:** replay is per-(layer,seq) independent — no pid_batch coupling, no cross-seq reduction, no atomics on the data path, all tl.sum reductions over fixed constexpr tiles within one program, disjoint per-seq bank-row writes → output bits independent of B and co-residents; the same #42960 N-independence class as the tl.range scan fix (beec984a/e4a6a2f2/45519178 lineage).

**Live gates:** (a) one-time scan-store-vs-replay byte A/B on captured payloads; (b) the standing gate "durable accepted state diff = 0 vs current publish" (the fr13_accept_only_publish_gate logic, moved on-line); (c) re-pointed scan_state_staging serving gate (the diag[12] probe is now vacuous — see risks); (d) final regime gate = B=4 CUDA-captured SWE-4 vs E5, per policy.
synthesis.risks_and_steppingstone:
**Stage-1 is a SEMANTIC stepping stone, mechanically ~half throwaway — keep it, but build the full route on the persistent-buffer plumbing, not the dict.** REUSED by the full route: the accept-only commit semantics + the adversarially-verified dead-row license (only non-diagnostic bank readers are the h0 gather patch :2474-2480 and the remap masked pid_k<accepted_len kernel :100-101) — exactly the license replay needs to never store rejected states; the committer-as-publish-point timing; the gate artifacts (scripts/fr13_accept_only_publish_gate.py, the committer-wiring test); and critically the pre-existing persistent accepted-path/lens device buffers (patch :184-201, filled :3624-3637) which ARE the replay kernel's inputs. THROWAWAY: the _FR10_PENDING_TREE_STATE_PUBLISH dict + committer index_copy_-from-tree_state (:2752-2761, :3649-3690, :4014-4055) — with no kernel scratch there is no tree_state to publish — and the ssm half of the remap (superseded by direct linear-column writes).

**BLOCKERS in stage-1 as written (one shared fix):** (i) the dict pins each layer's per-step tree_state_all (torch.empty :2020-2030) across the forward→sampler boundary, entries NEVER popped → ~48 x 201 MB ≈ +9.2 GiB steady-state, invisible to vLLM startup profiling → late OOM/KV pressure on GB10 unified memory; (ii) that buffer is per-step, NOT graph-stable — under the declared final-gate regime (B=4 FULL CUDA capture) per-batch-size graphs alias different allocations and the dict points at whichever was captured last = silent wrong-buffer publish (the diff's "graph-stable" comment is wrong); works today only because GDN runs eager/piecewise. Fix for both: ONE persistent preallocated staging bank per layer at init (the :184-197 pattern). The full route deletes the problem entirely (no scratch, ~50 MiB activation side-bank, no block-pool surgery).

**NEEDS-CARE:** (1) SILENT VACUOUS PASS — the diff neuters the staged-state probe (diag[12]/[13], :2824-2834) but scripts/fr10_serving_wiring_gate.py:38-39/:265-277 still gates scan_state_staging on diag[12]<=atol, which now sits at its zeros-init → gate passes with no evidence; re-point at _FR10_LAST_ACCEPT_ONLY_PUBLISH_ROWS + accepted-rows equality BEFORE merging stage-1 (fail-loud policy). (2) Stale-entry republish: pop on publish + assert entry count. (3) 192 eager torch.tensor(path) H2D + small launches per step on the sampler critical path — vectorize or absorb via Option 2. (4) h0/carrier: h0 column convention (bank col accepted_len-1) survives accept-only unchanged; the B=4 lossy carrier (conv/h0 bank-row + fp8 GEMM) is OUTSIDE the scan and untouched (ssm-only change) — but the full route must keep the conv remap half (:195-203; deleting it re-creates the FR13 conv-prior-window bug), still materialize the leaf state at the same column, carry a one-event-delayed prev-lens buffer for the replay base, and NOT consume intermediate linear columns without ordering (the remap has overlapping src/dst rows, benign today only because the sole consumed column's src is outside the write set). (5) Diagnostics/branch-oracle: serving captures embed scratch tree_state (:2649/:2733/:2773/:2812) and the FR12 splice copies INTO it (:2536-2555) — all env-gated OFF in deployment; under the full route guard them to raise/skip explicitly; the captures already store per-node q/k/v/g/beta so the branch oracle can recompute node states on CPU — the committer itself reads logits/token ids, never bank states. (6) Preemption/resume: a resumed request has no valid pending replay — define and assert the "no pending replay ⇒ bank state is final" invariant (re-read live vLLM preemption source first, per read-source-first). (7) Codegen identity is the one residual bit-exactness risk — covered by the shared-jit-body + byte A/B gate.
synthesis.verdict: **BANK stage-1, then build the full replay route — stage-1 alone does NOT suffice and going straight to full would discard a working de-risk.** Numbers: stage-1 = 1.385x traffic cut at a=4 (21.74 → 15.70 GB/forward; 5.14x → 3.71x actual native; 9x → ~6.5x on the doc's scale), degrading to 1.27x at a=5 and net-NEGATIVE (0.95x) at a=5 with a spilled committer temp — it removes only the rejected-row publish (6.04 GB) and leaves the kernel scratch store (5.44 GB), remap (4.83 GB), and h0 (0.60 GB) untouched.
